title: I lost my last paying client and decided to go all in on my brick breaking roguelike mining game, am I making a terrible mistake?
author: mattmirrorfish

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: For financial success? Definitely. Should have gone for a strong Player Fantasy in a popular Genre.

replies.author: mattmirrorfish
replies.body: Real. I did do some market research and saw that there seemed to be demand for mining games but then I might have gone off the rails with the roguelike hybrid nature of it kinda muddying the waters.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: fwiw, roguelikes are a very popular genre currently

replies.author: mattmirrorfish
replies.body: Yeah I’m a longtime roguelike player and dev for sure, my fave genre

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body: Say no to blinking screen, i can't look at it for more than few seconds.

replies.author: mattmirrorfish
replies.body: you are the third person now, duly noted! thanks

comments.author: jogalleciez
comments.body:
I knew this game looked generated. I played some of the demo and the only feedback I have is the onboarding is pretty rough. Tough to tell what the buttons do and upgrading was confusing to the point where I was just mashing Enter. 

You should post this to r/ClaudeGameDev too :)

replies.author: mattmirrorfish
replies.body: thanks! yeah it's still prototype mode, I need to do a real tutorial and much better onboard pass. Thanks a lot for trying it!

comments.author: OldLead4716
comments.body:
Yes horrible mistake.

You want to go all in on a already very and very oversaturated market. And that was before ai could one shot most basic gameplay loops .

replies.author: OldLead4716
replies.body: Keep at it for the passion . Hope you make some beer money.

comments.author: thegreatredbeard
comments.body: Reminds me of lovers in a dangerous space time for some reason.

replies.author: mattmirrorfish
replies.body: I'll take! That's a nice game

comments.author: C0L0SSUSvdm
comments.body: I'm sold on the gameplay/concept. IMHO, not a professional opinion, Idt I vibe with the aesthetic of it. So many colors, so small. Kind of going cross-eyed a little trying to follow what's going on, what the goal is supposed to be. It's the entire color spectrum packed into mostly tiny squares and some circles

replies.author: mattmirrorfish
replies.body: thanks! Glad the concept is resonating. I hear you about the visuals, I think at some point I may bring in someone who's better at pixel art and try to do an overhaul to make it more clear and readable. Right now just trying to gather feedback. Appreciate you taking the time!

comments.author: boxlinebox
comments.body: I can dig it. As a fan of both Arkanoid and Solar Jetman back in the day, this looks like their love child.

replies.author: mattmirrorfish
replies.body: Arkanoid was one of my fave arcade games as a kid, so satisfying. Thanks!

comments.author: blessed--
comments.body: yes you start this out as a hobby, get some success then quit your day job not the other way around.

comments.author: IbbyLives
comments.body: This looks great, my one note would be that the character doesn't match the environment's art style. As for your title, almost certainly. Unless you have some edge noone else has in the market you need to consider that you will likely do about average on release, and that doesn't make quitting your dayjob money. I'd still pursue it though! Just make sure you have a fallback too.
